metadata.description: An explicit edge to dbx-cli:build-base, NOT `^build`. This entry point compiles into the parent's dist directory, which `dbx-cli:build-base` deletes and rewrites (rollup `deleteOutputPath: true`), so it cannot run before the parent -- but the edge has to be spelled out, because `^build` here would resolve to dbx-cli:build, which depends on this very target: a hard cycle. That XOR is the whole design constraint -- either the children get `^build` or the parent aggregates them, never both. Aggregating is the side that keeps one writer per dist directory.  It imports @dereekb/util/eslint, another family's CHILD, which collapses to util:build. Cross-family deps point at the other family's ROOT `build`: a sibling family's child has no `build` of its own and writes into its parent's dist, so only the parent's `build` -- which runs the ESM finalize -- produces a finalized copy for TypeScript to resolve `exports` against.
